title: Episode-based feedback loop — close the loop between search and feedback
description: Make mmry get sharper with use, zero LLM. Every mmry search records an episode (query, returned_ids, ts, agent_ctx). mmry add --using <ids> closes the episode and bumps helpful_count on cited memories. Five derived feedback channels (explicit, implicit positive, implicit negative, co-return lift, drift decay) are pure SQL aggregates over episodes — no separate counter tables until volume forces denormalization. Architectural keystone: storage is a dumb append-only log; intelligence lives in retrieval as pure functions over the episode log.

title: Wire episode recording into search path
description: After SearchService::execute_search returns Vec<Memory>, write an episode row with the resolved query, returned memory ids, ts, and AGENT_CTX. Return episode_id alongside results so the CLI can surface it (and so HTTP API can stay byte-stable — episode_id is additive on the response envelope).

title: Add --using flag to mmry add to close episodes
description: mmry add accepts --using <id,id,...> [--episode <ep_id>]. If --episode omitted, default to most-recent open episode for the current AGENT_CTX session within last N minutes. Closes the episode by setting used_ids and bumps implicit helpful_count on the cited memories. CLI-only flag — HTTP API stays unchanged.

title: Learning deduplication - embedding similarity to find candidates, then LLM equivalence check before merging. Runs during extraction.
Remove unused crate dependencies from Cargo.toml files after HMLR removal (rig-core, ort NER models, etc)
mmry add silently drops nested metadata field from JSON payload
description: mmry add reads content/category/importance/expires_at/tags from the JSON payload at crates/mmry-cli/src/commands/add.rs:505-544 but never reads metadata. Memory is created with empty metadata at line 518; only agent_ctx is merged at line 519. Repro: printf '{"content":"x","metadata":{"foo":"bar"}}' | mmry add - → subsequent search returns metadata: {}. Hstry session-recall ingest had to work around this by stashing conversation_id in tags as conv:<id>. Fix: after the agent_ctx merge, extract obj.get("metadata") as object and merge each key into memory.metadata. Add round-trip test.

title: Disable cross-encoder rerank by default
description: rerank_enabled: true with BAAI/bge-reranker-base at crates/mmry-core/src/config.rs:519,521. In the hstry session-recall eval, hybrid+rerank scored 0.811 MRR vs hybrid-norerank 0.862 — five points lost — and cost ~25% more latency. The QA-passage reranker is mis-calibrated for "find me the conversation about X". Flip default to false; callers opt-in per request. Document the opt-in path in README.

title: Investigate why ingest body > 8KB degrades recall across all engines
description: In the hstry session-recall eval, ingest config full-20k is consistently worse than full-8k across every engine — including BM25 and SPLADE which should benefit from more text. Suspects: chunking aggregation, BM25/sparse vector dilution from trailing low-signal content. Likely partially entangled with the long-context embedding swap; investigate after that lands and reassess whether this still reproduces. title: Append-only workspace memory ledger (.mmry/mmry.jsonl) with optional daemon indexing
description:
Simplify mmry around a local append-only memory ledger at `.mmry/mmry.jsonl` as the durable source of truth. SQLite/embeddings/daemon search become derived indexes and convenience layers, not mission-critical storage. This aligns with the current lean refactor history: recent commits removed agents/facts/pruning/HMLR complexity, unified per-store DBs into one `mmry.db`, and already added AGENT_CTX metadata stamping.

## Context from codebase/history

- Current storage is SQLite (`memories`, `episodes`) with `Memory { content, metadata, tags, parent_id, store, helpful_count... }` in `crates/mmry-core/src/memory/types.rs`.
- `AgentCtx` already reads `AGENT_CTX_*` defensively and stamps `metadata.agent_ctx`, with indexed workspace/session columns.
- Recent simplification commits:
  - `54f5975` dropped agents registry, facts, pruning, TUI agent_events.
  - `027721e` unified per-store DBs into one `mmry.db` with `store` column.
  - `5ea261c` collapsed `--store all` fanout into a single WHERE-clause search.
  - `0d66e86` added AGENT_CTX support.
- Existing open epics (`mmry-xrbv`, `mmry-84c7`) assume a heavier DB/search-centric design. This epic should supersede or reshape those ideas rather than add another parallel subsystem.

## Desired architecture

`.mmry/mmry.jsonl` is the canonical local event log:

- Always readable/writable by sandboxed agents with ordinary repo file access.
- Append-only; stale/deprecated/replaced memories are new events, never in-place mutation.
- Human-inspectable, git/diff/copy friendly, repairable with standard tools.
- Optional daemon watches/ingests it into SQLite/FTS/BM25/sparse/dense indexes.
- CLI can operate directly on JSONL when daemon/index is unavailable.

The daemon/indexer is a derived cache:

- Rebuildable from JSONL.
- Can add embeddings, feedback aggregates, semantic search, compaction candidates.
- Failure should not prevent `mmry add`, `mmry list`, `mmry grep`, or `agntz context` from getting useful local memories.

## Initial event shape

Use a versioned JSONL event envelope, embedding existing AGENT_CTX as provenance:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "id": "evt_...",
  "ts": "2026-06-01T...Z",
  "type": "memory.add",
  "memory_id": "mem_...",
  "source": "user_stated|agent_inferred|tool_observed|imported|system_rule",
  "scope": "repo|workspace|user|global|session",
  "content": "...",
  "memory_type": "episodic|semantic|procedural",
  "category": "default",
  "tags": [],
  "metadata": {},
  "agent_ctx": {}
}
```

Lifecycle events to support early:

- `memory.add`
- `memory.deprecate`
- `memory.supersede`
- `memory.tag`
- `memory.feedback` / `episode.close` if episode loop survives
- `memory.snapshot` / `memory.compaction` for token-efficient active views

## Check-in policy and secret safety

Open design question: should `.mmry/mmry.jsonl` be committed? Proposed answer: default should be **not automatically committed** unless the store is explicitly initialized as shareable, because memories can contain user/project-sensitive context. If checked in, enforce a shareable-mode policy:

- initialize with `mmry init --shareable` or `mmry config set commit_policy tracked`;
- default `.gitignore` should ignore `.mmry/` or at least `.mmry/mmry.jsonl` for private stores;
- allow tracked team memories only after explicit opt-in;
- use external secret scanners first instead of building a bespoke scanner into mmry;
- integrate with `gitleaks` as the fast local/default scanner (`gitleaks protect --staged`, filesystem scans for `.mmry/`, `.trx/`, exports);
- optionally support `trufflehog` for slower/deeper or verified scans;
- scanner integration should be generic (likely `agntz secrets ...` or a shared byteowlz helper), so `.trx`, `.mmry`, hstry exports, sessions, and docs can all use it;
- mmry should call the generic scanner before shared writes / exports / commit-oriented workflows, and fail closed for tracked/shared memory files;
- reject scanner findings unless `--allow-sensitive` writes only to an ignored private file;
- store secret references (`kyz://...`, env var names), never raw secret values;
- include `sensitivity: public|internal|private|secret_ref` and `visibility: private|shared` / `commit_policy: trackable|private` per event;
- provide `mmry export --redact` and hook installation that delegates to the generic scanner.

## Implementation slices

1. Define schema in `../schemas/mmry/` for the event envelope and active memory projection.
2. Add core JSONL append/read module with file locking and corruption-tolerant reads.
3. Add CLI direct-mode commands: `mmry init`, `mmry add`, `mmry list`, `mmry grep/search-lite`, `mmry deprecate`, `mmry compact --dry-run` over `.mmry/mmry.jsonl`.
4. Stamp existing `AgentCtx` onto events as `agent_ctx`; add `source`/`sensitivity` fields.
5. Add external-scanner guardrails before shared writes and exports: delegate to generic `agntz secrets`/shared helper backed by `gitleaks` first, optional `trufflehog` deep scan later.
6. Teach existing SQLite database to ingest/rebuild from JSONL; make it a cache/index.
7. Make daemon optional watcher/indexer; CLI falls back to JSONL automatically.
8. Update `agntz context/tldr` plan to consume active JSONL projection plus optional indexed search.
9. Reconcile/close/supersede older heavier issues (`mmry-xrbv`, `mmry-84c7`, HMLR leftovers) after this architecture lands.

## Validation

- Sandbox smoke test: in a repo with no daemon and no mmry DB, `mmry add` writes `.mmry/mmry.jsonl` and `mmry list` returns it.
- Rebuild test: delete `mmry.db`; daemon/CLI rebuilds index from JSONL with identical active memories.
- Deprecation test: add + supersede/deprecate yields correct active projection without mutating old lines.
- Secret guard test: with `gitleaks` available, shared writes/exports containing common API key/token/private key patterns are blocked or redacted by default; private ignored writes may require explicit `--allow-sensitive`.
- Git policy test: private init adds ignore rules; shareable init permits tracking and still scans.

title: mmry add-conversation: ingest hstry canonical conversation JSON as N message records
description:
Add a new subcommand `mmry add-conversation` that accepts the canonical byteowlz conversation shape (as emitted verbatim by `hstry --json show <id>`) and writes one mmry record per message, with session-level linkage so retrieval can dedup back to the conversation.

## Motivation

Eval data (hstry/eval/runs/20260517-201154/summary.md) shows:
- mmry-sparse @ full-8k: MRR 0.829 — best non-rerank
- mmry-semantic plateaus at MRR 0.357 across full-2k/8k/20k

Root cause for the dense plateau: today we ingest one mmry record per session with the full transcript glued together. That squashes a multi-topic conversation into a single 384-dim vector — topic dilution by design. Token-level engines (BM25, SPLADE) tolerate it; dense cannot.

mmry already has a text chunker (chunking/mod.rs, default max_chunk_tokens=200) but it is generic — it splits on `\n\n` cascading to sentences/words. It does not know about message boundaries, so it may coalesce two short turns or split a long assistant turn mid-thought, and the resulting chunks share the parent's session-level metadata (no role, no per-message timestamps, no position).

hstry already has clean message boundaries via `messages: [{role, content, created_at, ...}]`. We should use them.

## Canonical shape (already exists, do not invent a new one)

`hstry --json show <id>` returns the canonical byteowlz conversation JSON. Top-level keys observed:

```
external_id, readable_id, title, created_at, updated_at,
model, provider, workspace, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd,
messages[], metadata, version, message_count,
id, harness, platform_id, source_id   (hstry-internal extras, ignore or pass through)
```

Each message:

```
role, content, created_at, model?, tokens?, cost_usd?,
parts?, tool_calls?, metadata?
```

Reference Rust types: hstry/crates/hstry-runtime/src/runner.rs:161-233 (ParsedConversation, ParsedMessage, ParsedToolCall, ExportConversation). Same shape exists on TS side in hstry/adapters/types/index.ts. This is shipped, stable, and exercised by every adapter (claude-code, hermes, FRUM, codex, …).

## Proposed CLI

```
hstry --json show <id> | mmry add-conversation --store hstry-sessions -
mmry add-conversation --store X /path/to/conversation.json
mmry add-conversation --store X --json '{"...": "..."}'
```

Flags mirror `mmry add` where it makes sense (--store, --importance default 5, --category-from workspace, --dry-run, --json output).

## Storage policy (one valid first cut)

For each input conversation, write:

1. One **session header** record with `content = title` (or first user message if title is empty), metadata block carrying session-level fields (external_id, workspace, model, provider, harness, etc.), tags `["hstry-session", "source:<source_id>", "harness:<harness>", "conv:<external_id>"]`.

2. N **message** records, one per element of `messages[]`:
   - `content = "[<role>] <message.content>"` (or just the content — bikeshed later)
   - `parent_id = <session header memory id>` (reuses the existing parent_id column)
   - metadata: `{role, msg_index, created_at, model, tokens, cost_usd, conv_id: <external_id>}`
   - tags: same `conv:<external_id>` so retrieval can dedup without joining

Long messages (> max_chunk_tokens) still go through the existing chunker; chunks inherit parent_id from the message record. This gives a clean hierarchy: session → message → chunk.

Retrieval at the caller side groups by `conv:<external_id>` and surfaces best-matching message per conversation. (See also mmry-93vp for standardizing search output and a possible future `--group-by parent_id` flag.)

## Out of scope for this ticket

- Codegen'd JSON Schema from the hstry types (nice-to-have, separate ticket if you want a machine-readable contract for non-Rust/TS consumers).
- Reranker / hybrid weight tuning (covered by mmry-z8tj, mmry-fn0n).
- Embedding model swap (covered by mmry-qxyn — once chunks are message-sized, the existing MiniLM 512-ctx model has a real shot, so qxyn may de-prioritize after this lands).
- `--group-by parent_id` flag on search (separate ticket).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by mmry-bntt (metadata-drop bug) since this feature relies on metadata round-tripping correctly. add-conversation should write metadata directly through the database/operations.rs path, not the broken JSON-payload path in commands/add.rs, but the underlying bug should be fixed regardless.

## Validation

After this lands, hstry/scripts/test-mmry-session-ingest.sh becomes the reference caller and the overnight eval re-runs. Expected outcomes:
- mmry-semantic MRR moves off the 0.357 plateau (focused message-sized vectors).
- mmry-sparse and mmry-bm25 stay strong or improve (more, smaller, focused records).
- mean_ms drops for full configs (no more 20K-char single payloads).

## Reference files

- mmry/crates/mmry-cli/src/commands/add.rs (model the new command after this, but bypass the metadata-drop bug at line 505-544)
- mmry/crates/mmry-core/src/chunking/mod.rs (reuse for in-message chunking only)
- mmry/crates/mmry-core/src/database/operations.rs (existing parent_id support is the right primitive)
- hstry/crates/hstry-runtime/src/runner.rs:161-233 (canonical type definitions)
- hstry/eval/runs/20260517-201154/summary.md (eval that motivated this)

title: Remove legacy indexed/intelligent cruft; keep only append-only workspace ledger
description:
## Goal

Finish the mmry simplification once and for all. Make `.mmry/mmry.jsonl` the only source of truth and remove the legacy indexed/intelligent product hidden inside mmry.

`mmry` should be a tiny deterministic workspace memory ledger. It stores explicit, distilled memories and replays append-only events. It should not run models, extract memories, consolidate learnings, manage a search daemon, ingest conversations, or duplicate `vqtrs`, `hstry`, QMD, and wiki responsibilities.

## Keep

- `mmry init [--tracked]`
- `mmry add <text|->`
- `mmry list` / `mmry ls`
- deterministic lexical `mmry search`
- `mmry rm` as an appended deprecation event
- `mmry doctor`
- JSON output
- `mmry-core::MemoryFile` and the append-only event schema
- agent/source metadata already carried deterministically in events
- migration tooling needed to export legacy data into JSONL, with a documented removal horizon

## Remove

- `--indexed` paths and legacy SQLite stores/migrations.
- `mmry-service`, gRPC/protobuf service code, daemon lifecycle, and service discovery.
- `mmry-tui` and `mmry-mcp` if they depend on the legacy indexed backend; do not port them in this issue.
- embedding, sparse embedding, reranking, fuzzy/hybrid weighting, and vqtrs client code from mmry.
- analyzer/model configuration, LLM extraction, consolidation, reflection, deduplication judgment, and heuristic extraction fallback.
- conversation/session ingestion and hstry watcher integration.
- cross-store/federation features tied to the old database model.
- obsolete config fields, schemas, dependencies, install steps, docs, tests, and binaries.

## Issue reconciliation

Audit open issues and close/supersede those incompatible with this decision, including the extraction/consolidation/indexed-search direction (`mmry-xrbv`, `mmry-w6q5`, `mmry-kj8d`, `mmry-sfxf`, `mmry-9sc1`, `mmry-rd15`, embedding/search-service issues, and episode work that exists only for the legacy backend). Preserve only issues that clearly deepen the append-only MemoryFile interface.

Update `mmry-j1te` so its accepted target is the lean ledger without an optional indexing daemon.

## Design constraints

- No model calls in core or CLI.
- No heuristics that decide what is important.
- No hidden global store in the default product.
- No graceful fallback from intelligent extraction to worse heuristics; the capability simply does not belong here.
- Other tools may read the JSONL or call the CLI, but mmry does not become their orchestration layer.

## Migration

- Provide one explicit, tested command/script to export every supported legacy memory into workspace JSONL.
- Report unsupported/lossy fields before migration.
- Never silently discard active memories.
- Document backup and rollback steps.

## Proof of positive outcome

1. Workspace contains only the core/CLI crates required for the lean ledger; legacy service/TUI/MCP/indexed crates are removed from the workspace.
2. `rg -n "indexed|EmbeddingService|SparseEmbedding|rerank|analyzer|consolidat|mmry-service|mmry-tui|mmry-mcp" crates README.md Cargo.toml` finds no live legacy implementation except clearly marked migration documentation.
3. CLI help exposes only the lean ledger commands.
4. Migration tests prove representative legacy records become valid replayable JSONL without silent loss.
5. Tests cover init, append, replay, lexical search, deprecate, malformed lines, concurrent append safety, and tracked/untracked setup.
6. `cargo check --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, and `cargo test --workspace` pass.
7. README is concise and describes one product, not legacy and new modes.
8. Obsolete TRX issues are closed/superseded and linked to this cleanup epic.

title: Add fast cross-repository list/search over distributed JSONL ledgers
description:
## Goal

Add fast cross-repository discovery and aggregation while preserving one append-only `.mmry/mmry.jsonl` source of truth per repository.

This is convenience only: no global memory database, daemon, synchronization layer, semantic index, or duplicated records.

## CLI

```bash
mmry list                         # current repository
mmry search "release"             # current repository
mmry list --repo trx              # one discovered repository
mmry search "release" --repo trx
mmry list --all                   # aggregate all discovered repositories
mmry search "release" --all
mmry repos                        # list discovered names and canonical paths
```

`--repo` and `--all` must be mutually exclusive.

## Configuration

Use the normal XDG config file, with CLI flags taking precedence:

```toml
[[roots]]
path = "~/byteowlz"
max_depth = 2

[[roots]]
path = "~/work"
max_depth = 2
```

Update the mmry JSON schema so roots receive validation and LSP completion. Do not silently search the entire home directory by default.

## Discovery

- Resolve `~` and canonicalize configured roots.
- Discover directories containing `.mmry/mmry.jsonl` within bounded `max_depth`.
- Skip `.git`, `target`, `node_modules`, hidden cache directories, and symlink loops.
- Repository display name defaults to directory basename.
- `--repo <name>` fails loudly when no match or multiple matches exist; ambiguous errors list canonical candidate paths.
- `mmry repos` shows whether each memory file exists and is readable.

## Aggregation

- Replay each JSONL file independently using `mmry-core::MemoryFile`.
- Merge results in memory only.
- Include `repo` and canonical `repo_path` attribution in human and JSON output.
- Preserve deterministic ordering with an explicit stable tie-break (for example timestamp descending, then repo path, then memory id).
- A malformed repository file should produce a repository-attributed error; do not silently omit it.

## Performance

Keep this boring first: bounded discovery plus parallel file reads should be sufficient. Do not add a daemon or persistent global index without measured evidence.

Add a benchmark/fixture covering at least 500 repositories with small JSONL ledgers. Record cold runtime and ensure the implementation does not traverse excluded dependency/build trees. If discovery is measurably slow, add only a rebuildable path-manifest cache with explicit invalidation; it must never become a memory source of truth.

## Non-goals

- Cross-repository writes or replication.
- A global memory file/database.
- Embeddings, reranking, or semantic search.
- Automatic extraction or consolidation.
- Repository catalog ownership beyond configured-root discovery.

## Proof of positive outcome

1. Tests cover current repo, named repo, all repos, zero match, ambiguous names, malformed JSONL, symlink loops, excluded directories, and stable ordering.
2. JSON output includes repository attribution.
3. The generated config schema validates `roots.path` and `roots.max_depth`.
4. A benchmark over 500 fixture repositories completes within a documented target on a normal development machine; report the measured result rather than asserting speed.
5. `cargo check --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, and `cargo test --workspace` pass.
6. No global database/service/index is introduced.

## Relationship

Child of `mmry-sz23`. This capability must survive the legacy cleanup because it deepens the lean distributed-JSONL product rather than reintroducing the old indexed backend.

description: Default search weights at crates/mmry-core/src/config.rs:523-528 are: keyword 0.4, fuzzy 0.2, vector 0.35, bm25 0.0, sparse 0.0. In the hstry eval, standalone scores are sparse 0.829, bm25 0.789, keyword 0.480, vector 0.357, fuzzy 0.357 (worst). BM25 and SPLADE — the two strongest engines — are weighted zero in the default hybrid pipeline, while fuzzy (the worst engine) gets 20%. Proposed defaults: bm25 0.30, sparse 0.30, vector 0.20, keyword 0.15, fuzzy 0.05. Hybrid-norerank MRR should hold ≥ 0.86 on full-8k after change.
